correctness.rationale: Polynomial vanishing on x^2+y^2=1 forces F=omega Jp+(R-1)G with degree F=degree G+2. The exact periodic adjoint identity s=-(omega/2)h_prime-kh with k=p·G and s=Jp·G follows by differentiating the phase PDE in radial direction. If k has nonzero highest Fourier frequency N>=1, the leading coefficient of kh at m+N forces e^{iθ}(k+is) to have frequency m+N+1; if k is constant and m>=1, imaginary coefficient -(im omega/2+k)h_m is nonzero and forces m+1. The m=0 case uses nonzero mean radial damping to force degree G>=1. Thus degree F>=m+3, and equality makes k constant. The explicit H=(kappa h-omega h_prime)/2 harmonic polynomial makes radial ODE rdot=kappa*r*(1-r^2)/2 and linear transverse exponent -kappa; its adjoint matches Z. Independent SymPy test verified m=4 h=2sin2θ-2sin4θ, exact phase adjoint, logistic radial identity, degree seven.
